headline: Steady, not cheap: eastern-suburbs family homes keep rising slowly while rates sit still
outlook: Adelaide's inner-east has outperformed the national market for three years and the school-zone premium in Linden Park and Glenunga has widened. Stock is slightly higher than last spring, which is giving buyers a little more choice, but well-presented family homes on full blocks still sell inside three weeks. With the cash rate on hold and only one or two cuts priced for 2027, borrowing capacity is unlikely to jump; price growth should stay in the low single digits.
timing: There is no strong reason to wait. A 25-50 bp rate cut in 2027 would lift borrowing capacity by roughly 3-5%, and sellers in this pocket tend to price that in quickly. Buy when the right house appears, negotiate hard on anything that has been listed more than four weeks or has already dropped its guide, and keep a buffer for rates staying higher for longer.
